explanation: Performance optimization in computer systems aims to improve the speed and efficiency of program execution.  This involves understanding the hardware-software interaction, utilizing the memory hierarchy effectively, and minimizing bottlenecks.  Optimizations can target various aspects, including algorithm design, data structures, and low-level code manipulation to leverage the underlying architecture.
syntax: No single strict syntax; optimization techniques vary depending on the specific performance bottleneck.  They may involve algorithmic changes, data structure choices, compiler optimizations, or even low-level assembly language modifications.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates performance optimization through algorithmic choice. Code fragments A and B perform the same computation but have different asymptotic performance. Fragment C shows the most efficient approach by pre-calculating min and max values. These different approaches highlight how choosing appropriate algorithms and minimizing function calls can drastically impact performance by reducing the number of instructions executed and the amount of data accessed in memory, thereby affecting cache utilization and CPU cycles.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
